Beginning Monday, President Trump will have a new White House chief of staff as he was
leaving the White House Friday.
The president said Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, the architect of some of the
president's most controversial policies, is being promoted.
The move comes after Tuesday's midterm election Republican losses.
NPR's Michelle Kurtzleben has more.
You could read these losses as a clear repudiation of Trump's policies, but then
Miller is a true mega believer.
I mean, he's been with the president since his 2016 campaign.
He's always been considered one of the chief architects in particular of the
president's hardline immigration policies.
So this seems to be the administration, the administration saying full speed ahead.
Democrats are criticizing Miller's appointment.
The House Minority Leader, Hakim Jeffery, said Miller needs to be fired instead of
promoted. The backlash against President Trump's immigration enforcement tactics
played a role in this week's Republican losses, especially in Texas.
NPR's Sergio Martinez Beltran reports Democrats are weighing a seismic
political shift.
Exit polling shows immigration was top of mind for voters in Texas.
Two men have been killed by ICE agents, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in
Houston, who was shot to death on his way to work.
His son, Ronaldo Salgado, says the results should make the new Democratic majority
reflect. Unfortunately, Texas has become like the epicenter of ICE enforcement
and like gross violence against immigrants and the voters spoken.
The incoming lawmakers have a duty to listen to to us.
Locally, immigrant rights advocates say they want the state to stop collaborating
with ICE. Nationally, they want less funding for ICE and oversight.
Sergio Martinez Beltran, NPR News, Austin, Texas.
The faculty Senate at Cornell University issued a vote of no confidence against the
school's administration on Friday.
Yanyung Hahn of Member Station WSKG reports the resolution
rebucks the school officials about how they have handled sexual assault on the
campus. The no confidence measure passed with 75 voting in favor and 50 opposed.
Faculty at Cornell proposed the resolution after a former student referred to as
Jane Doe filed a lawsuit saying she was gang raped at a fraternity house in 2024.
Faculty say the university failed to protect Doe and others from campus sexual
violence. Co-sponsors of the resolution say they've lost faith in the ability of
Cornell's administration to handle this issue.
Cornell's President Michael Kotlikoff declined to comment, but the board of
trustees issued a statement saying they are confident in his leadership.
The school appointed former U.S.
Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to conduct an independent investigation.
For NPR News, I'm Jung Yoon Hahn. And this is NPR News.
Three weeks after having a portion of lung removed during cancer surgery in Rome,
Pope Leo has begun a three nation tour of Latin America starting in Uruguay.
The 71 year old Pope says he felt better than he looked and he credited God, his
medical staff and his healthy lifestyle for a rapid recovery.
Chilean students are back in the streets as tension builds over a government
decision to reduce the sentences of a certain set of prisoners from the capital
Santiago. John Bartlett has more.
Amid angry clashes between protesters and police in the capital Santiago,
Chile's students are taking aim at Justice Minister Fernando Rabat as the backlash
over a controversial set of pardons threatens to spiral out of control.
Chile's far right President Jose Antonio Cast and his government are under fire
after 56 people convicted of a range of crimes from sexual abuse to the rape of
minors, as well as two prisoners charged with human rights violations suddenly saw
their prison sentences reduced by government decree.
Cast's approval rating has plummeted as anger builds.
Yet upon his return from a European tour, he signaled that he will back Rabat.
This wave of protests, meanwhile, shows little sign of abating.
For NPR News, I'm John Bartlett in Santiago, Chile.
Elon Musk says Tesla will begin next year to end the production of its electric
Cybertruck. In a post on X, he said the decision was made to make room to produce
more of the autonomous vehicle, the CyberCab.
The Cybertrucks cost $82,000 for the base model, up to $102,000 for the top of the
line. This is NPR News.
